title: Move run, attempt and decision records from D1 into .ticfac/ on the run branch
description:
SPEC 12 Phase 4 item 6. Move run/attempt/decision records out of D1 and into .ticfac/ on the run branch, pushed to origin at once (SPEC 10.4); leave D1 as a rebuildable index, or remove it.

READ 9da BEFORE STARTING. This item makes that defect worse, not better: 9da is the close-out deadlocking because the run's checkpoint writes move the PR head it gates CI on, and this item moves MORE records onto that same branch. Phase 3 hit it with checkpoints alone; with attempts and decisions there too, every record written during a close-out re-invalidates the CI it is waiting for.

So this tick does not start with a migration. It starts by establishing how run-state writes and the PR + CI gate coexist - whether records go to a ref that is not the PR's head, whether CI is asked about the last non-run-state commit, or whether the close-out stops writing while it waits. Then migrate.

The prize is real and worth the care: records in git are readable by a resumed run with no database, which is what makes a Workflow restart recoverable.

acceptance_criteria: Run, attempt and decision records live in .ticfac/ on the run branch and a resumed run reads them with no D1 access. D1 is either rebuildable from them or gone. An epic close-out still reaches a CI verdict with these writes happening - the 9da interaction is demonstrated as resolved, not assumed.
